client_brief:
Evergreen Provisions: Recovered Evergreen crest system

Project overview
Evergreen Provisions runs two dispensary shops in Bend, built around six house strain families. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Recovered Evergreen crest system and Evergreen capsule capture set.

What we will provide
evergreen_crest_panels/ (6 frames, roughly 4200 x 4200); evergreen_garment_blanks/ (5 frames); evergreen_spec_card_2024.pdf; evergreen_plate_schedule.csv; evergreen_ink_book.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Recovered Evergreen crest system: Six crests recovered from photographs of hand painted panels as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, compound lockups complete rather than missing their centre...
- Evergreen capsule capture set: Six panel captures brought to one capsule palette across two shooting visits, and five garment blanks corrected to their honest colours so ink contrast decisions made against them can be trusted, plus one licensed camera scale counter surface frame graded...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$2,500-$6,000 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork apparel capsule post quoted in this line's ledger grounding_note, from a vertically integrated cannabis retailer asking for 'a production-ready apparel design system for a branded retail capsule' that 'hands cleanly to manufacturers and decorators (vectors, tech packs)', in an 'elevated streetwear' direction, on palette with no rework. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional dispensary Evergreen Provisions (a generic dictionary pairing, no trademark collision), and the post's stated purple and black palette is dropped along with its from scratch garment art and embroidery digitising, which the ledger's own triage concedes are not connector work. What survives is the half that client genuinely needed and could not get: a decorator will not quote from a photograph, so the commission is recovery of the artwork that already exists into per ink plate art, plus the spec the shop floor actually works from. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that the honest fuller commission rather than a thin one, because an ink level trace off photographed painted collateral recovers real artwork, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the separation sheets and the teaser set, and the InDesign convert and merge chain turns the decorator's own last season spec card PDF into a live per design run. Verdict STRENGTHEN honoured: the concept and the six item collateral set are kept intact and the depth is raised from what sat on one vector surface to five honestly counted ones.

price_band_and_audience: Craft dispensary lifestyle capsule at 32 dollars a tee and 70 dollars a hoodie, buyer 25 to 45, bought at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. The band is load bearing. At this price the painted origin is the product, so the plates have to retain brush edge, dry brush breakup and a halftoned paint field, and the palette stays earthy and limited to the inks the decorator already keeps on his shelf. Flatten those crests into clean geometric marks with a mass retail two ink treatment and the capsule reads as gas station merch, which will not hold 70 dollars. Push the other way into a foiled, sparse, monogrammed designer drop look and it misprices a counter sold 32 dollar tee and stops looking like the panels on the wall, which is the only reason the customer walked over. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every plate separates correctly. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A vertically integrated cannabis retailer running two dispensary storefronts, launching a short-run counter-sold apparel capsule.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Bend, Oregon. Two owned dispensary shops, owner-run, with a small counter-retail apparel line.
brand_identity.about: Evergreen Provisions runs two dispensary shops in Bend, built around six house strain families. Two years ago the owners paid a local sign painter to hand-paint a crest panel for each family onto the shop walls. Customers photograph them constantly and ask where they can buy them, and the first apparel capsule exists to answer that question without losing the hand that made the panels.
brand_identity.audience: Craft-minded dispensary customers aged 25 to 45 who buy at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. People who pay for the painted origin, not for a logo.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tees at 32 dollars, hoodies at 70 dollars, short-run and counter-sold. Elevated streetwear priced above gas-station merch and below a designer drop. The painted texture is the product, so the value sits in the brush surviving, not in gloss or foil.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a painted or brushed-character face that echoes the sign painter's hand, kept legible. Support and spec type in a plain workhorse sans so the plates and sheets read cleanly. Type never competes with the painted crest.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain-spoken, shop-floor honest. No luxury posturing and no carnival hype. Example line: "These are hand painted panels and that is the entire reason anyone wants them. Keep the brush in it, and tell us plainly what came back and what did not."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The six crest panels were hand-painted by a local sign painter who has since moved to Montana and left no sketches or files. The only surviving artwork is a set of bench photographs of the finished panels, shot over two visits under mixed light. There is no vector art and no separation art, which is exactly why the screen printer cannot quote a run.
brand_identity.values: Craft and honesty. Keep the painted hand, hold the palette to the inks the decorator already stocks, and say plainly what the paintings can and cannot give a screen.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_crest_panels/ (6 frames, roughly 4200 x 4200)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photographs of six hand painted crest panels on primed board, taken on the shop bench across two separate visits under mixed daylight and counter light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six panels as they hang on the wall. Two were shot on a different day so they sit a little different."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six are compound lockups, a ring of painted lettering around a central sprig, and a single compound selection returns the ring and the outer arcs while silently dropping the sprig at full success. One panel is painted in a deep aubergine that sits within a hair of the stained board behind it, so an ink level selection there has almost no contrast to work with, and the dry brush hairlines and the small painted caps are barely open in the paint itself, so whether they survive a trace is a property of each panel rather than of the tracing.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_garment_blanks/ (5 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs of the actual blanks the shop stocks: three tees (bone, heather olive, black) and two hoodies (black, oat), laid on the counter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The blanks we carry, shot on the counter so you can see the real colours."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They were shot under warm counter lights, so the black hoodie photographs brown and the heather olive reads yellow, which makes every judgement about ink contrast on those grounds wrong until the frames are corrected. One of the five was shot on a hanger rather than flat and sits noticeably off level.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_spec_card_2024.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The decorator's own spec card artwork from last season's run, supplied as the press PDF his floor already recognises: job name, ink list, plate order, placement and print width.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer wants us to use. Same layout as last year, he says just fill it in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's four blocks read as visually separate on the printed page but the PDF's text is one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes a frame granularity nothing like the printed page suggests. The mapping readout also omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past it is short, and the validator still reports the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_plate_schedule.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Six rows written by the shop: design name, garment, garment colour, placement, print width in inches, and the ink count as the shop guessed it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Designs, garments, placements and the widths our printer gave us over the phone."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One row is a sleeve hit at a print width a small fraction of the chest widths, and two rows name the same crest on two different garment colours, which is one design and two plate sets rather than two designs. The ink counts are the shop's guesses and are not derived from the art.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_ink_book.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text list of the stock inks the decorator keeps on his shelf, with the shop's own notes on which ones they like.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The inks he already has. Anything off this list costs us a mixing charge."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether these particular traces still hold at the width they actually print, on the garment colour they actually print on. The paintings carry dry brush hairlines and small painted caps whose counters are barely open in the paint itself, and the tracer takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster prep upstream. At canvas scale every trace looks clean and complete. The sleeve hit prints at a fraction of the chest widths, and whether its counters close and its hairlines drop out at that size, against olive or against black rather than against white, is a property of that one painting meeting that one reproduction size and is not reported by anything.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer does not exist until the plate has been traced and laid down at its true width on the corrected garment ground, and there is no tracer parameter that would have prevented it. Nothing in the brief or the schedule states it: the schedule gives print widths because a decorator needs print widths, not as a warning about counters. It is not a propagation re run either, because the response is a different route for that design, either rebuilding the plate as a masked and flattened solid before tracing so the stroke carries weight, or accepting a coarser reduction for that placement and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster prep for the affected designs, rebuild those plates through a mask and flatten route rather than tracing the painterly stroke directly, re trace, redo the vector hygiene, and re judge every affected design at its stated width on its stated ground before any of it reaches a sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A capsule where the sleeve design prints as a plugged blob and the small painted caps close up on press, discovered by the decorator after screens are burned, on a capsule whose entire premise is that the brush survived.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construct the separation sheets are built on. A separation sheet shows each ink as its own layer sitting over the ones beneath it so the decorator can read the overlap and the trap. Authored the natural way that is a blended or partially transparent stack, and the importer discards the blend outright and returns a plain opaque shape, at full success and with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so every sheet after the first can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of the authoring, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for one piece of art per ink and says nothing about how a sheet is drawn. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction, either separating the plates spatially into registered panels with a printed offset key, or baking the overlap into a raster upstream so the trap is part of the picture rather than of the layout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the separation roots around whichever construction survives, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every sheet from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Separation sheets handed to a decorator on which the top plate covers the ones beneath it, so every design appears to be a one ink job, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the decorator's spec card actually is once converted, as opposed to what its printed face suggests. Its four blocks read as separate on paper, but the conversion decides the frame granularity and can collapse a continuous flow into a single frame, so there may be no separate name frame and ink frame to map fields to at all. Compounding it, the readout the mapping tool returns omits a run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, and the validator returns valid with no warnings on offsets that are wrong.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that controls it, because the granularity is a property of how that PDF was made and the readout's omission is invisible in the readout. Nothing states it: the client says only that the printer wants the same card again. It is not a propagation re run, because the correct response is a different mapping strategy computed from a different source of truth, the reconstructed story text from the round tripped document rather than the tool's own readout, plus a decision about which fields the exposed frames can carry at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute every offset from the reconstructed story text, re prepare the template, verify by a second round trip that each field placeholder is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message, re merge, and where two blocks collapsed into one frame decide which fields move into the note instead.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A spec card run that reports success, renders the right number of pages, and reaches the decorator's floor with the ink list and the plate order silently missing from every card.

decision_gates: How many inks each painting is actually worth on a 32 dollar tee, given that the ink counts in the schedule are the shop's guesses and every extra screen is real money.
Which parts of the brush earn a halftoned paint field and at what radius, and which parts must stay crisp.
Polarity before tracing, and whether the deliverable is the two colour trace or the masked and flattened colour accurate plate, decided per design rather than once.
What survives in a one colour reduction when two inks of similar value are left with one screen between them.
Whether two rows naming one crest on two garment colours is two designs or one design with two plate sets, and how that changes the card count.
How a separation sheet shows overlapping inks so a decorator can read the trap between plates.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a craft counter capsule rather than a corporate merch programme, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Which fields the converted spec card can actually carry, once its exposed frames are known, and which move into the note instead.

verifiers_process.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_process.how: Compare the pixel dimensions of every delivered file against its source per the manifest, and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_process.text: No image on any canvas resolved to the importer's placeholder, and each crest arrived as vector path shapes rather than as a single picture.
verifiers_process.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for 1x1 placeholder image data and count path shape elements in each crest's region.

verifiers_process.text: On every separation sheet each plate is independently present in the returned markup rather than covered by the plate above it.
verifiers_process.how: Read per element fill, opacity and geometry on each separation root and confirm each declared plate resolves to its own visible element.

verifiers_process.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_process.how: Read the font-family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_human.text: The six panels read as one capsule palette rather than as six paintings shot on two days.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the six graded masters in a row and judge white point, black point and paint hue as a set.

verifiers_human.text: Each crest still reads as a hand painted panel rather than as a flattened corporate logo.
verifiers_human.how: View each plate set composited at print size beside the original panel photograph and judge brush edge, dry brush breakup and paint field.

verifiers_human.text: At the print width the schedule states, on the garment colour it prints on, each crest keeps its hairlines and its counters stay open.
verifiers_human.how: Place each design at its stated width on the corrected blank for that row and view at that size, including the sleeve hit.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a 32 dollar tee and 70 dollar hoodie craft capsule, not as mass retail merch and not as a designer drop.
verifiers_human.how: Judge palette, ink count, type scale and treatment density against the stated band and buyer.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the shop and the decorator something they did not already know, including everything that could not be recovered or produced.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every reconciliation, every ink decision and every limitation is named.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pretty crests. IDENTITY: these are one named sign painter's six actual panels, hanging on the wall of two shops, that customers already photograph. A regenerated crest is a different painting, and the entire commercial premise of the capsule is that the customer recognises the thing on the wall. SPEC: a decorator burns screens off one piece of art per ink, with correct polarity, a real viewBox, no ground rectangle and open counters at a stated print width on a stated garment colour, none of which a generated image is or can be checked for, and a press PDF whose page count equals the reconciled design count is a hard count rather than a picture. EDITABILITY: the sheets and teasers are defined by being editable, because the drop date and the featured design will move and a two person shop cannot re commission. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this trace keep its hairlines at sleeve width on black, did the plate under the top one survive the import, did the field the tool said it wrote actually land in the template.
